newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: U.S. REJECTS CALL TO PROTECT SLOVAKIA IF NEUTRAL.
newsitem.headline: U.S. REJECTS CALL TO PROTECT SLOVAKIA IF NEUTRAL.

text.p: The United States on Tuesday rejected a request by a top Slovak politician for U.S. security guarantees should Slovakia declare official neutrality.

The U.S. embassy in Bratislava issued a statement following a meeting on Monday between Ambassador Ralph Johnson and Jan Slota, leader of the ultra-right Slovak National Party (SNS), who asked if such a guarantee would be possible.

"(The ambassador) explained that (the U.S.) recognises and respects other countries' declarations of neutrality," the statement said. "The Ambassador said he believes that the U.S. would not support a security guarantee of this kind."

The SNS is a member of Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's coalition government which has declared its official intention to be among the first former Soviet bloc countries to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).

However, the junior members of the broad coalition, the SNS and the leftist Workers' Party (ZRS), have opposed membership in both NATO and the European Union and the SNS has floated the idea of Slovak neutrality backed by superpower guarantees.

Western diplomats have all but ruled out Slovakia's chances of being included in the group of former communist countries expected to be invited to join NATO at a July summit in Madrid because of shortcomings in democratic reforms.
On Friday and Saturday Slovaks will vote in a referendum on whether or not the country should join NATO.
The ZRS and SNS have come out against NATO membership, while Meciar's Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) has adopted a lukewarm attitude towards the referendum.
Earlier this month, Slota discussed possible Slovakian neutrality with Russia's ambassador to Bratislava, Sergei Zotov, who promised Russian support.
"We directly asked ambassador Zotov for a possible Russian reaction to Slovak requests for neutrality guarantees...and we received a positive answer," Slota said.
Ambassador Johnson repeated U.S. support for Slovakia's official ambitions to join western structures.
"The United States would like to see Slovakia qualify for early entrance into NATO and other western structures," the U.S. statement said.
"The most important consideration for NATO members as they consider Slovakia's NATO candidacy will be whether Slovakia has demonstrated a commitment to democracy," the statement added.
